documents.title: Guidelines for Faculty in Dealing with the Use of Generative AI Tools
tiers: AI use is allowed in the course with proper referencing
AI use is allowed for specific assignments with proper referencing
documents.summary: Provost guidelines for faculty explain what generative AI is and where it errs, then advise faculty to experiment, talk with students, redesign assignments and put a syllabus statement in place. It ends with three suggested syllabus statements that instructors can adopt.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no rule of its own for all courses; it offers three suggested syllabus statements ("AI use is allowed in the course with proper referencing", "AI use is allowed for specific assignments", "AI use is not allowed") for instructors to choose. Per the codebook, offering tiers or templates means delegates.

units.why: Defines the technology the guidelines cover: "Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) is a computer-based technology that creates a variety of data". It sets the scope of the document, so it is a definition (P61), general phase, informs.
units.anchor: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) is a computer-based technology that creates a variety of data

units.why: States the purpose and audience of the document: "offering guidelines to faculty on using these tools in the classroom as they continue to evolve". A framework preamble for faculty, so P56 rather than a rule.
units.anchor: offering guidelines to faculty on using these tools in the classroom

units.why: Warns that output is unreliable: "You cannot rely on ChatGPT-generated content for research, learning and education." This is the verify-output family (P31); it says not to rely, so should-not.
units.anchor: You cannot rely on ChatGPT-generated content for research, learning and education

units.why: Names bias as a limitation: "All users need to be aware of the inherent bias of these generative AI tools". Ethical and bias concern for everyone, so P53, informs.
units.anchor: All users need to be aware of the inherent bias of these generative AI tools

units.why: Invites faculty to try tools: "Faculty may experiment with generative AI tools in conjunction with their course materials and assignments." Supports faculty learning before setting policy (P63); it is permissive, so may.
units.anchor: Faculty may experiment with generative AI tools in conjunction with their course materials and assignments

units.why: Advises faculty to "integrate the tool or develop alternative approaches that do not require it" after testing their assignment prompts. This is assignment redesign around AI (P35).
units.anchor: you should consider how you can integrate the tool or develop alternative approaches that do

units.why: Recommends "involving students in the reflection process" about tool advantages and limitations. This is explaining and discussing AI with students (P66), not a syllabus rule.
units.anchor: involving students in the reflection process can provide a valuable learning experience

units.why: Guideline 2 tells faculty to "Talk with students about these generative AI tools explicitly". Discussion beyond a syllabus line, so P66.
units.anchor: Talk with students about these generative AI tools explicitly

units.why: Faculty should "Invite them to collaboratively consider and establish learning goals and criteria for the task, with consideration for the role of AI". Setting expectations together with students is P67 (co-create); P66 fits less because the students help decide.
units.anchor: Invite them to collaboratively consider and establish learning goals and criteria for the task

units.why: Says "You should clarify the principles and guidelines for using generative AI tools in your courses". Communicating expectations to students; P66 (explain the rules) fits better than P09 because the verbal clarification is separate from the syllabus recommendation.
units.anchor: You should clarify the principles and guidelines for using generative AI tools in your courses

units.why: "we recommend a syllabus statement on using AI" asks instructors to put AI expectations in the syllabus. Recommended, not required, so should; type P09.
units.anchor: we recommend a syllabus statement on using AI
units.fit_note: The document recommends a syllabus statement; it does not require one.

units.why: Tells faculty to "Discuss the ethical issues and limitations of AI with your students", including inaccurate or biased output. Explaining and discussing AI with students, P66; the ethics content is secondary.
units.anchor: Discuss the ethical issues and limitations of AI with your students

units.why: Guideline 3: "Create assignments that are not easily completed using AI". Assignment redesign, P35.
units.anchor: Create assignments that are not easily completed using AI

units.why: "provide clear instructions to students regarding the proper citation of generative AI tools in their assignments" is a recommendation that instructors set up citation of AI use, so a disclosure rule (P24) addressed to instructors.
units.anchor: provide clear instructions to students regarding the proper citation of generative AI tools in their
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors (highly recommended) rather than directly to students.

units.why: "Students should be required to explain how they utilized these tools in their work" asks for a student account of how AI was used, which is a reflection on use (P26) rather than only a citation.
units.anchor: Students should be required to explain how they utilized these tools in their work

units.why: Suggests "more opportunities for in-class presentations" to build oral skills and shift assessment to student explanation. Closest is P34 (demos where students explain work).
units.anchor: you may provide more opportunities for in-class presentations
units.fit_note: Presented as building oral communication skills, not explicitly as checking understanding of AI-assisted work.

units.why: Guideline 4 says instructors "may incorporate a formative assessment practice where students are required to submit drafts of their work for review and feedback". Process-based redesign (P35); drafts also serve to detect plagiarism per the text.
units.anchor: students are required to submit drafts of their work for review and feedback

units.why: Guideline 5: "Familiarize yourself with University policies and guidelines on the use of Generative AI." A duty to stay informed about institutional guidance, P102.
units.anchor: Familiarize yourself with University policies and guidelines on the use of Generative AI

units.why: The heading "Suggested Syllabus Statements on AI Use" introduces three ready-made statements (allowed with referencing; allowed for specific assignments; not allowed). Named options for instructors to pick from, P05; the document stance is therefore delegates.
units.anchor: Suggested Syllabus Statements on AI Use
units.policy: Three suggested syllabus statements are offered: AI use allowed with proper referencing; AI use allowed for specific assignments with proper referencing; AI use not allowed.
units.fit_note: Options are labelled by allowance; the document does not call them tiers.

units.why: Template 1 says "Students are welcome to explore approved generative AI tools to seek support for their assignments". Welcoming default use in the course, P02; "approved" tools are a condition.
units.anchor: Students are welcome to explore approved generative AI tools to seek support for their assignments

units.why: Template says students "should follow the 'verify everything' approach to the content generated by these AI tools". Output can be wrong, so P31.
units.anchor: students should follow the “verify everything” approach to the content generated by these AI tools

units.why: The template makes the student answerable for plagiarism risk: "responsibility to check the original sources to be sure they are not plagiarizing someone else's work". Ownership of what is submitted (P29); P31 would fit the checking, but the point is student responsibility.
units.anchor: responsibility to check the original sources to be sure they are not plagiarizing someone else’s

units.why: Explains why: "These tools learned the models from the public internet, which means they may reproduce substantial text from other sources." A fact about output risk supporting the verify rule, P31, informs.
units.anchor: they may reproduce substantial text from other sources

units.why: "cross-check the content and citations generated by these tools to ensure they are accurate" directs verification of AI output and its references, P31.
units.anchor: cross-check the content and citations generated by these tools to ensure they are accurate and

units.why: "Students should incorporate the subsequent statement in their assignments when using a Generative AI Tool" requires a disclosure statement with each submission, P24.
units.anchor: Students should incorporate the subsequent statement in their assignments when using a Generative AI Tool

units.why: The template statement names "[Generative AI Tool Name], a language model created by [Generative AI Tool Provider]" and purposes of use, so the disclosure must include tool, provider and purpose: P25.
units.anchor: [Generative AI Tool Name], a language model created by [Generative AI Tool Provider]
units.fit_note: Requires tool, provider and purposes, but not the prompt or output.

units.why: Points students to the "UA AI Experience" as "a helpful resource for understanding responsible and informed engagement with generative AI". Offers AI-literacy material to students, P70.
units.anchor: Students may find the UA AI Experience

units.why: Template 2: "Students are allowed to use approved generative AI tools for specific assignments, as designated by the instructor." AI is decided per assignment, so P04; permit unit stance.
units.anchor: Students are allowed to use approved generative AI tools for specific assignments, as designated by

units.why: Template 3: "All submitted work must be produced by the students themselves, whether individually or collaboratively." Submitted work must be the student's own, P29.
units.anchor: All submitted work must be produced by the students themselves

units.why: Template 3 bans every use: "Use of any generative AI tool in this course constitutes academic misconduct under UA's Academic Misconduct Policy." I chose P01 (default ban) over P36 because the sentence defines the ban for all work in the course; the misconduct label is secondary.
units.anchor: Use of any generative AI tool in this course constitutes academic misconduct
units.fit_note: Also classifies the ban as misconduct under the Academic Misconduct Policy (P36).

documents.title: Use of Generative AI in Comps, Theses and Dissertations
tiers: permitted for brainstorming, bibliographic searches and graphics (editing allowed)
permitted for data analysis and computation
permitted for developing, writing, debugging and proofreading code
documents.summary: The Graduate School charges each program to set its own limits on generative AI in committee-based exams, theses and dissertations. It states shared expectations (student responsibility, oral defense, disclosure, data privacy) and gives four sample program statements from open use to a full ban.
documents.stance_why: The "Charge to departments" says "Each graduate program should develop specific parameters regarding the degree to which the use of generative AI is allowable", and four example statements range from permitted uses to "not permitted at any phase". The document supplies templates and hands the decision to programs and committees, so delegates; it only discourages over-reliance.

units.why: The charge says each graduate program "should develop specific parameters regarding the degree to which the use of generative AI is allowable". The Graduate School hands the decision to programs, P85, addressed to administration.
units.anchor: the degree to which the use of generative AI is allowable

units.why: "students are responsible for the full content of the document" regardless of how it was composed: students own what they submit (P29).
units.anchor: students are responsible for the full content of the document

units.why: Students must show in the oral defense "their ability to engage with the concepts and evidence provided in the document". Understanding is checked by oral defense (P34).
units.anchor: expected to demonstrate, in the oral defense, their ability to engage with the concepts and

units.why: "the primary responsibility of authorship resides with the student" keeps the student as principal author and thinker, P32.
units.anchor: the primary responsibility of authorship resides with the student

units.why: "over-reliance ... on generative AI is strongly discouraged" discourages without forbidding; the limit is defined by discipline and committee. P03.
units.anchor: on generative AI is strongly discouraged

units.why: Gives the reason for authorship by the student: "the development and mastery of advanced academic skills is expected not only during the degree program but throughout the scholar's subsequent professional career". Skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: Because the development and mastery of advanced academic skills is expected not only during the

units.why: Defines generative AI as "artificial intelligence systems that can create new content, including text, images, audio, video, code, or data outputs" and lists tools. Definition and scope, P61.
units.anchor: that can create new content, including text, images, audio, video, code, or data outputs

units.why: The definition names "AI coding assistants (e.g., GitHub Copilot, CodeWhisperer)" as covered tools, extending the guidance to editor-integrated assistants (P07).
units.anchor: AI coding assistants (e.g., GitHub Copilot, CodeWhisperer)
units.fit_note: Only names coding assistants as in scope; no rule on disabling them.

units.why: The scope covers "AI writing assistants that generate substantive content beyond basic grammar/spelling correction", implicitly leaving basic grammar and spelling correction out. Nearest type is P100 (routine features exempt).
units.anchor: AI writing assistants that generate substantive content beyond basic grammar/spelling
units.fit_note: Exemption is implied by the scope definition rather than stated as a rule.

units.why: States "Different academic disciplines will have distinct expectations regarding the level to which the exam/thesis/dissertation process can or should be aided by generative AI". Allows rules to differ by discipline, P85.
units.anchor: Different academic disciplines will have distinct expectations regarding the level
units.fit_note: Variation is by discipline and program rather than by school.

units.why: Lists "Some examples of generative-AI-integrated work" (brainstorming, literature review, data analysis, code, translation, editing, full chapters) for programs to consider. A menu of use categories, nearest P05; it does not allow or forbid any of them.
units.anchor: Some examples of generative-AI-integrated work might include
units.policy: Examples of generative-AI-integrated work include initial brainstorming, initial literature review, development of theoretical framework, design of research methodology, data analysis, data transcription and coding, generation of graphics or video, generation of audio content, generation of software code, translation, proofreading/editing/revision, and generating full paragraphs/pages/chapters.
units.fit_note: A list of kinds of use, not named tiers; no stance is attached to the items.

units.why: "A thorough disclosure of how generative AI was used ... is required of all students who submit generative-AI-integrated work." Required disclosure with the submission, P24.
units.anchor: A thorough disclosure of how generative AI was used

units.why: "students are expected to adhere to the guidelines of their degree program": students must follow the rules of their own program, P78.
units.anchor: students are expected to adhere to the guidelines of their degree program

units.why: "Faculty members should remain attentive to work that is technically inconsistent or unusual, that may signal inappropriate use" tells faculty which signals to weigh. Evidence for suspicion (P69), not a detector.
units.anchor: Faculty members should remain attentive to work that is technically inconsistent or unusual
units.fit_note: Names a signal to watch for, not a standard of proof.

units.why: "Unauthorized use of generative AI tools for scholarly work may be considered an offense under UA's Academic Misconduct Policy and/or Research Misconduct Policy." Classifies unauthorized use as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Unauthorized use of generative AI tools for scholarly work may be considered an offense

units.why: "All users need to be aware of the potential inaccuracies, fabrication of sources and citations, and biases of generative AI tools". Output can be wrong and biased, P31.
units.anchor: potential inaccuracies, fabrication of sources and citations, and biases of generative AI tools

units.why: "Departments may adopt a shared policy on the use of generative AI" for committee-based exams and theses. Units set their own rules, P85.
units.anchor: Departments may adopt a shared policy on the use of generative AI

units.why: "variation from a department-wide policy is permissible, but should be documented": decisions can differ per thesis, so the committee decides case by case (P04), with a duty to document.
units.anchor: variation from a department-wide policy is permissible, but should be documented
units.fit_note: Also requires the variation to be documented and shared with the committee.

units.why: "The guidance to students should be provided as early as possible in the student's research or exam-preparation work." Timing of communicating expectations; P09 is the nearest communicate type.
units.anchor: The guidance to students should be provided as early as possible
units.fit_note: Sets timing for giving guidance, not a requirement to state it in a syllabus.

units.why: Footnote: "We encourage departments to share their policy statements ... with each other, so that best practices in this arena can be shared." Peer exchange between units, nearest P88.
units.anchor: We encourage departments to share their policy statements
units.fit_note: Sharing is among UA departments, not with outside peers or partners.

units.why: "current copyright regulations around generative-AI-produced content are unclear": a copyright caution for students, P52, informs.
units.anchor: current copyright regulations around generative-AI-produced content are unclear

units.why: "Copyright violations might also occur when AI supplies text from unattributed sources." Copyright risk of AI output, P52.
units.anchor: Copyright violations might also occur when AI supplies text from unattributed sources

units.why: "future detection tools might point towards generative-AI-sourced text that was inaccurately documented by the student author" warns that later detection may expose poorly documented use. Nearest P40.
units.anchor: future detection tools might point towards generative-AI-sourced text
units.fit_note: A warning about future detection, not a statement that detectors are used now.

units.why: "Limitations regarding future publication may arise" notes consequences for publishing manuscripts that used AI: research and scholarship, P62.
units.anchor: Limitations regarding future publication may arise

units.why: Example statement 1: "The use of generative AI is permitted for brainstorming, initial bibliographic searches, and the production of graphics". Brainstorming permission, P15.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI is permitted for brainstorming, initial bibliographic searches, and the production
units.fit_note: Also permits bibliographic searches and graphics, which no listed type covers.

units.why: "The student is responsible for verifying all bibliographic information, and for any omissions; this responsibility cannot be transferred to generative AI." Verify AI output, P31.
units.anchor: The student is responsible for verifying all bibliographic information

units.why: "Students are also responsible for ensuring that information from generative AI has not been plagiarized from some other source". Verification of AI output for plagiarism, P31.
units.anchor: responsible for ensuring that information from generative AI has not been plagiarized from some other

units.why: "Students are responsible for writing the exam/project/thesis/dissertation manuscript themselves": AI may not produce the submitted manuscript, P19.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for writing the exam/project/thesis/dissertation manuscript themselves

units.why: "generative AI may be used for editing" explicitly permits editing support on the manuscript, P91.
units.anchor: generative AI may be used for editing

units.why: "Entire paragraphs written by generative AI ... are not allowed" even with student prompts: a ban on AI-generated text submitted as one's own, P19.
units.anchor: Entire paragraphs written by generative AI
units.policy: Entire paragraphs written by generative AI, even if from student-submitted prompts, are not allowed.

units.why: Gives the reason for the paragraph ban: students "are expected to develop and refine their own independent scholarly voice and style". Skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: students (with faculty mentorship) are expected to develop

units.why: "Students are expected to include a Generative AI Disclosure Statement in the opening pages of the manuscript": a statement placed in the submission, P24.
units.anchor: include a Generative AI Disclosure Statement in the opening pages of the manuscript

units.why: Example statement 2: "The use of generative AI is permitted for data analysis and computation, as well as for research." Data analysis permission, P89.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI is permitted for data analysis and computation

units.why: "students are responsible for the accuracy and completeness of all information generated by AI": verify AI output, P31.
units.anchor: students are responsible for the accuracy and completeness of all information generated by AI

units.why: Example statement 3: "The use of generative AI is permitted for developing/writing/debugging/proofreading code". AI-generated code allowed under the conditions that follow, P16.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI is permitted for developing/writing/debugging/proofreading code
units.fit_note: Also covers debugging and proofreading code.

units.why: "responsible AI-assisted coding is itself a graduate learning objective": the program treats effective AI use as something it teaches, P44.
units.anchor: responsible AI-assisted coding is itself a graduate learning objective
units.fit_note: Framed as a learning objective, not as a career expectation.

units.why: Students are to use AI "to deepen technical understanding rather than bypass learning": AI must not replace their thinking, P32.
units.anchor: using them to deepen technical understanding rather than bypass learning

units.why: Students should show "maturity in deciding when AI assistance is appropriate versus when independent implementation is required". The student remains the decision-maker, P32.
units.anchor: demonstrate maturity in deciding when AI assistance is appropriate versus when independent implementation is required

units.why: "employing AI to explore design options and prototype solutions" is named effective use: exploring approaches, P15.
units.anchor: employing AI to explore design options and prototype solutions

units.why: Students should evaluate AI code "for correctness, efficiency, security, ethics, reproducibility, and maintainability": verify AI output, P31.
units.anchor: for correctness, efficiency, security, ethics, reproducibility, and maintainability

units.why: "ensuring clarity and documentation through human-readable logic, comments, and version control" sets quality expectations for AI-assisted code that no type covers; it is not marking AI-derived code (P27).
units.anchor: ensuring clarity and documentation through human-readable logic, comments, and version control
units.uncovered_note: Code quality and maintainability practices expected of AI-assisted code (readable logic, comments, version control).

units.why: "Students must be able to explain and justify their coding decisions": explain every part of what is submitted, P30.
units.anchor: Students must be able to explain and justify their coding decisions

units.why: "document AI assistance, and demonstrate full conceptual command and independent authorship": requires documenting AI help, P24.
units.anchor: document AI assistance, and demonstrate full conceptual command and independent authorship
units.fit_note: Disclosure is paired with a demand to show independent authorship.

units.why: "students remain fully responsible for the validity, originality, and functionality of all code submitted": ownership of submitted work, P29.
units.anchor: students remain fully responsible for the validity, originality, and functionality of all code submitted

units.why: "AI may enhance rigor, creativity, and capability, but it cannot replace disciplinary expertise, academic integrity, or critical thinking": AI must not replace student thinking, P32.
units.anchor: it cannot replace disciplinary expertise, academic integrity, or critical thinking

units.why: Example statement 4: "The use of generative AI is not permitted at any phase of the exam/project/thesis/dissertation work." A full ban, P01.
units.anchor: The use of generative AI is not permitted at any phase of the exam/project/thesis/dissertation work

units.why: "Use of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT in the research, writing, or revision ... constitutes academic misconduct": misuse is classed as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: constitutes academic misconduct

units.why: "All students who use generative AI during the exam/project/thesis/dissertation process must include a disclosure statement": disclosure with each submission, P24.
units.anchor: must include a disclosure statement

units.why: "the exact nature of which should be agreed upon between the student and the faculty at the start of the project": the form of disclosure is set jointly at the start. Nearest P67 (setting expectations with students).
units.anchor: the exact nature of which should be agreed upon between the
units.fit_note: Student and faculty agree the disclosure format, not the whole AI policy.

units.why: The sample statement names "[Generative AI Tool Name and version/date], a language model created by [Generative AI Tool Provider]": disclosure includes tool, version or date and purpose, P25.
units.anchor: the author has utilized [Generative AI Tool Name and version/date]
units.fit_note: Tool, version/date and purposes, but no prompt or output.

units.why: "Students should be made aware that most professional publication outlets will also require such a statement." Research publication norms, P62.
units.anchor: most professional publication outlets will also require such a statement

units.why: "documenting from the outset the ways in which generative AI was used, is of the utmost importance": keep a running record of AI use, nearest P26.
units.anchor: documenting from the outset the ways in which generative AI was used
units.fit_note: Asks for documenting from the start but does not name transcripts or logs.

units.why: Quotes a journal policy: "Authors need to disclose the use of generative AI and AI-assisted tools in their work." External publication rule on disclosure, P62.
units.anchor: Authors need to disclose the use of generative AI and AI-assisted tools in their work

units.why: "Students must ensure that any data entered into generative AI tools complies with UA policies including IRB protocols, data use and software licensing agreements": data and privacy, P50.
units.anchor: Students must ensure that any data entered into generative AI tools complies with UA policies
units.fit_note: Framed as compliance with existing policies (P77) as well as privacy.

units.why: "Sensitive, proprietary, or identifiable information should not be uploaded to commercial AI platforms without appropriate safeguards": protect personal data, P50.
units.anchor: should not be uploaded to commercial AI platforms without appropriate safeguards

units.why: "Usage must also comply with UA's Office of Information Technology list of approved and prohibited AI tools": use approved tools only, P92.
units.anchor: list of approved and prohibited AI tools

units.why: Usage must comply with "Office of Research & Economic Development policies regarding intellectual property as well as data governance policies": comply with existing university policy, P77.
units.anchor: Office of Research & Economic Development policies regarding intellectual property

units.why: "the current guidance should not be interpreted as discouraging student projects that advance the research, development, or application of generative AI": research on AI itself is welcome, P62.
units.anchor: should not be interpreted as discouraging student projects that advance the research, development, or application
units.fit_note: Concerns research about AI rather than use of AI in the thesis process.

units.why: "Faculty and graduate students are encouraged to participate in these training opportunities" offered by the UA Teaching Academy on ethical use and disclosure: training, P70.
units.anchor: Faculty and graduate students are encouraged to participate in these training opportunities

units.why: Names the ad hoc committee (Graduate School deans, faculty from Anthropology, Computer Science, Information Systems, a PhD student) that wrote the guidance: how the policy was made, P84.
units.anchor: Ad Hoc Committee on Generative AI Use in Graduate Committee-Based Exams,

documents.title: AI Hub FAQ on the Generative AI Policy
documents.summary: The AI Hub FAQ summarizes the May 2026 Generative AI Policy as guardrails on data, contracts and approved tools. It says faculty decide classroom use, must put an AI statement in each syllabus, and that misuse is handled as academic misconduct; it also covers researchers and staff.
documents.stance_why: The FAQ says "The policy does not dictate classroom use" and "Faculty have discretion to set course-level expectations, which can range from prohibited to encouraged with disclosure." It sets no course-level stance of its own and passes the decision to instructors, so delegates, with a required syllabus statement.

units.why: "The Generative AI Policy provides guardrails, not roadblocks, so the UA community can use AI confidently, responsibly and securely." Institution-wide purpose statement, P56.
units.anchor: The Generative AI Policy provides guardrails, not roadblocks

units.why: "The policy does not dictate classroom use; it focuses on the data, contracts and integrations behind the tools." Leaves classroom decisions to instructors, nearest P04.
units.anchor: The policy does not dictate classroom use
units.fit_note: Says what the policy does not cover; the instructor-level delegation is stated separately in the instructor FAQ.

units.why: "Use approved tools when working with UA information": use university-approved tools, P92.
units.anchor: Use approved tools when working with UA information

units.why: "keep sensitive data out of unapproved platforms": protect confidential data, P50.
units.anchor: keep sensitive data out of unapproved platforms

units.why: "submit new tools to OIT for review before they touch university systems": review before deployment, P65.
units.anchor: submit new tools to OIT for review before they touch university systems

units.why: "The University recognizes generative AI as a valuable resource for instruction, research and administration." States a benefit and answers "Is UA banning AI tools? No." P87.
units.anchor: The University recognizes generative AI as a valuable resource for instruction, research and administration

units.why: "Approved tools listed on the AI Hub may be used with appropriate oversight." Permits approved tools, P92.
units.anchor: Approved tools listed on the AI Hub may be used with appropriate oversight

units.why: "The University encourages responsible experimentation while emphasizing ethical use, academic integrity, data privacy and compliance". An encouraging overall stance, P02.
units.anchor: The University encourages responsible experimentation

units.why: "faculty and staff input is essential as the University monitors AI use and adjusts guidance over time": guidance will change and input is invited, P54.
units.anchor: the University monitors AI use and adjusts guidance over time

units.why: "Many AI tools transmit user inputs to third-party systems and may use that data for training or may store the data." Explains why tools are reviewed, P50.
units.anchor: Many AI tools transmit user inputs to third-party systems and may use that data for

units.why: "Security, legal and accessibility standards are met." Names the review criteria for tools, P65.
units.anchor: Security, legal and accessibility standards are met

units.why: "Review focuses on initial acquisition and higher-risk uses, especially those involving sensitive data, contracts or system integrations." Scope of tool review, P65.
units.anchor: Review focuses on initial acquisition and higher-risk uses

units.why: "Free or public AI tools may collect, store or use input in ways that do not align with UA's data protection requirements." Privacy risk of free tools, P50.
units.anchor: Free or public AI tools may collect, store or use input in ways that do

units.why: "users should avoid registering for third-party AI platforms with a university email unless the tool has been approved or recommended by UA": a data-handling rule, P50.
units.anchor: users should avoid registering for third-party AI platforms with a university email

units.why: "UA employees may not use personal AI accounts for University business." A rule on operational AI use, P76.
units.anchor: UA employees may not use personal AI accounts for University business

units.why: "report suspected security issues to the IT Service Desk": a duty to report AI-related security problems, P71.
units.anchor: report suspected security issues to the IT Service Desk

units.why: "Submit a request on the Technology Security and Compliance Review Portal" is the route for tool review, P65.
units.anchor: Submit a request on the

units.why: "Faculty must include a statement on their syllabi regarding the use of Generative AI tools": a mandatory syllabus statement, P09.
units.anchor: Faculty must include a statement on their syllabi regarding the use of Generative AI tools

units.why: "faculty may determine whether and how AI is used in their courses, set expectations for students and document those expectations in the syllabus": instructor decides, P04.
units.anchor: faculty may determine whether and how AI is used in their courses

units.why: "Use of AI in coursework should rely on approved tools." Coursework AI should use approved tools, P92.
units.anchor: Use of AI in coursework should rely on

units.why: "Faculty have discretion to set course-level expectations, which can range from prohibited to encouraged with disclosure." Per-course choice across a range, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty have discretion to set course-level expectations
units.fit_note: Also names the range of positions (prohibited to encouraged with disclosure).

units.why: "they can choose from 3 prepopulated options provided in Simple Syllabus": ready-made options, P05.
units.anchor: choose from 3 prepopulated options provided in Simple Syllabus
units.fit_note: The three options are not described in this document.

units.why: The syllabus statement should address "Whether AI use is permitted, restricted or prohibited overall." Content requirement for the statement, P09.
units.anchor: Whether AI use is permitted, restricted or prohibited overall

units.why: The syllabus statement should say "Which approved tools may be used." Content of the statement, P09.
units.anchor: Which approved tools may be used

notes: Coder B. Only the three included university-layer documents were coded; no school or computing-unit policy was found, and the full May 2026 Generative AI Policy text was not available (the FAQ stands in for it). Graduate School text contains ligature characters (e.g. 'specific'), so some anchors were chosen to avoid them. Repeated syllabus-template paragraphs in the provost guidelines (template 2 verify/disclosure text, UA AI Experience link) were coded once as exact repeats. Template 3 sentence 'Use of any generative AI tool in this course constitutes academic misconduct' was coded P01 rather than P36 because it defines the ban.
